title: Cap for a thin-walled tube
prompt:
All dimensions are millimetres. Build exactly what is described — no fillets, chamfers, draft or extra features unless the description asks for them. Leave the finished part in the document; do not export anything.

An end cap for a round tube. The tube stands with its axis on Z, centred on that axis: 30 outside diameter, 2 wall, its top face at Z = 40.

Make the cap that closes that end. It slips OVER the outside of the tube: a skirt whose bore is 30.4 (so 0.2 of clearance all round), 12 deep, and above it a solid top 3 thick whose underside lands on the tube's end face. The cap's outside diameter is 36.

Build it where it sits on the tube — the skirt from Z = 28 to Z = 40 and the top from Z = 40 to Z = 43 — not at the origin.

inputs.why: the tube the cap has to fit. The GRADER mates against it; the agent is told its dimensions in prose and never gets the file, because a task that hands over the geometry is asking for a boolean, not a design

checks.why: a cap big enough to clear anything would pass every clearance check ever written
the cap's top lands ON the tube end, so they touch — a cap floating above it is not a cap
a slip fit: 0.2 of clearance all round means the two solids do not share space
the tube's end annulus is 176 mm2 and the cap has to be sitting on it
the skirt bore, at the size that makes the clearance
